objective_for_doctor: A 0-year-old M patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: fever.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I have a fever and a cough.

Dr. Agent: How long have you had the fever and cough (days), and what is the highest temperature you’ve measured?  
Dr. Agent: Do you have any trouble breathing, wheezing, or fast breathing, and how is your feeding/urination in the past 24 hours?
I don’t know.

Dr. Agent: I’m going to check your breathing now—can you look comfortable and tell me if you have any grunting or flaring of the nostrils; also, is the cough dry or wet?  
Dr. Agent: Since you don’t know the duration or temperature, I need a quick exam: I’m listening for wheezes/crackles—any chest pulling in when you breathe?
I don’t know.

Dr. Agent: I’m checking your chest and oxygen level—please tell me if you’re breathing very fast, if your ribs pull in with breaths, or if you look very sleepy or won’t feed.  
Dr. Agent: Also, do you have any runny nose, vomiting/diarrhea, or has anyone around you been sick recently?
I don’t know.

Dr. Agent: I’m going to listen to your lungs and check your vital signs—please tell me if you can drink/feed at all, and whether you have any fewer wet diapers than usual in the last day.  
Dr. Agent: Also, do you have a rash, stiff neck, or are you hard to wake?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I’m going to examine your oxygen level and breathing rate now—please look calm; is your chest pulling in between the ribs or are your lips/face bluish at all?  
Doctor: Also, when I touch/press your ear and throat area, do you seem in pain, and do you have any swollen glands or reduced tears when crying?
I don’t know.

Doctor: Since you don’t know, I need to check right now—please keep still while I measure your temperature, count your breaths for 30 seconds, and check oxygen saturation; does anything hurt when I touch your chest or throat?  
Doctor: Next, I’ll decide what tests are safest—can you request/confirm any recent immunizations (especially pneumococcal/Hib) and whether this is the first day of symptoms or longer?  
Doctor: I’ll also request a basic workup to clarify the cause if you’re not improving—REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry_and_Vitals, Chest_X-Ray, CBC_with_Differential, Respiratory_Viral_PCR.
I don’t know.

Doctor: While we wait, tell me: is the baby under 3 months old, and are there any danger signs right now like not feeding, lethargy, or fewer wet diapers?
I don’t know.
